common_name: Let's Dance Hydrangea (Compact Reblooming Bigleaf Hydrangea Series)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Let's Dance is a compact, reblooming bigleaf hydrangea series that flowers on both old and new wood, giving reliable summer bloom even after a late frost damages the previous year's buds.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, protected from hot afternoon sun. Let's Dance is a breeding series of compact, reblooming bigleaf hydrangeas that stay under 3 feet tall, considerably smaller than older mophead cultivars, while still flowering on both old wood from the previous season and new wood produced the same year. This reblooming trait means a late spring frost that kills the old flower buds does not prevent a good summer bloom, unlike older hydrangea cultivars that flower only once per year on old wood. Individual cultivars within the series vary in flower form (mophead or lacecap) and color. Flower color shifts with soil pH the way most macrophylla hydrangeas do, ranging from blue in acidic soil to pink in more alkaline soil, and can be adjusted with soil amendments. Keep soil consistently moist, since hydrangea's large leaves wilt quickly in dry heat, and prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since heavy pruning removes the old-wood flower buds that provide the earliest bloom flush.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Reblooming Hydrangea Series
Bailey Nurseries — Let's Dance Hydrangea Series Notes

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Twist-n-Shout is a reblooming lacecap hydrangea in the Endless Summer series, producing flattened flower heads of tiny fertile florets ringed by larger showy sterile florets, on plants that flower on both old and new wood.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, protected from hot afternoon sun. Twist-n-Shout, part of the Endless Summer series, is a reblooming lacecap hydrangea producing flattened flower clusters with a center of small, star-shaped fertile florets surrounded by a ring of larger, showier sterile florets, a more delicate, airy look than the round pompom flowers of mophead types. It flowers on both old wood from the previous season and new wood produced the same year, so a late spring frost that damages old buds does not prevent a strong summer and fall bloom. Deep red-tinted stems provide additional interest even when the plant is not in flower. Flower color shifts with soil pH the way most macrophylla hydrangeas do, ranging from blue in acidic soil to pink in more alkaline soil, and can be adjusted with soil amendments. Keep soil consistently moist, since the large leaves wilt quickly in dry heat, and prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since heavy pruning removes the old-wood flower buds that provide the earliest bloom flush.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Cityline is a compact bigleaf hydrangea series bred for a dense, tidy, rounded habit and strong stems that hold up large mophead blooms without flopping, well suited to smaller gardens and container culture.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, protected from hot afternoon sun. Cityline is a series of compact bigleaf hydrangeas, named for individual cities, bred for a dense, rounded, well-proportioned habit that stays under 3 feet and holds its large mophead blooms upright on strong stems rather than flopping under the flower weight, a common problem with older, taller hydrangea cultivars. Its compact size makes it especially well suited to foundation plantings, small gardens, and large containers where a full-sized hydrangea would be too large. Individual cultivars within the series bloom in shades from blue and purple to pink and red depending on soil pH, ranging from blue in acidic soil to pink in more alkaline soil, adjustable with soil amendments. Keep soil consistently moist, since the large leaves wilt quickly in dry heat, and prune lightly if needed, since bloom occurs primarily on old wood formed the previous season and heavy pruning removes next year's flower buds.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; BloomStruck is an Endless Summer series hydrangea bred for improved heat and sun tolerance, sturdier red-tinted stems, and better disease resistance than older reblooming cultivars.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; BloomStruck tolerates more direct sun than most bigleaf hydrangeas, though afternoon shade is still beneficial in the hottest Gulf South summers. Part of the Endless Summer series, BloomStruck was bred for improved heat tolerance, sturdier dark red-purple stems, and better resistance to powdery mildew than older reblooming hydrangea cultivars, along with vivid rose-pink to purple mophead flowers that shift with soil pH. It flowers on both old wood from the previous season and new wood produced the same year, so a late spring frost that damages old buds does not prevent a strong summer and fall rebloom. Flower color ranges from blue-purple in acidic soil to rose-pink in more alkaline soil, and can be adjusted with soil amendments. Keep soil consistently moist, since the large leaves wilt quickly in dry heat, and prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since heavy pruning removes the old-wood flower buds that provide the earliest bloom flush.

common_name: Mini Penny Hydrangea (Dwarf Reblooming Blue Mophead Hydrangea)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade; Mini Penny is a dwarf sport of the reliable reblooming cultivar Penny Mac, staying compact enough for small gardens and large containers while retaining its parent's dependable rebloom.

directions: Plant in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, protected from hot afternoon sun. Mini Penny is a dwarf sport of the widely grown, reliably reblooming Penny Mac hydrangea, retaining its parent's strong performance — flowering on both old wood from the previous season and new wood produced the same year — while staying considerably more compact, typically under 2 feet tall, making it well suited to small gardens, foundation plantings, and large containers where a full-sized hydrangea would be too large. Because it reblooms on new wood, a late spring frost that damages old buds does not prevent a strong summer bloom. Flower color shifts with soil pH the way most macrophylla hydrangeas do, ranging from blue in acidic soil to pink in more alkaline soil, and can be adjusted with soil amendments. Keep soil consistently moist, since the large leaves wilt quickly in dry heat, and prune only lightly to remove dead wood, since heavy pruning removes the old-wood flower buds that provide the earliest bloom flush.
